title: 2024 Electricity Consumption Analysis Report
executive_summary: This report details electricity consumption for 2024 based on 1,428 smart-meter readings totaling 1,207,700 kWh. Industrial usage dominated consumption, while overall usage increased by 4.7% in the second half of the year. A significant negative correlation was found between temperature and commercial energy use.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 1,428 readings with a total consumption of 1,207,699.96 kWh, averaging 845.73 kWh per reading.
Industrial usage was highest at 995,362.16 kWh, followed by Commercial (196,367.15 kWh) and Residential (15,970.65 kWh).
Consumption was highest in Q4 (352,881.81 kWh) and lowest in Q3 (264,863.12 kWh).
Total consumption increased by 4.71% from 589,955.03 kWh in H1 to 617,744.93 kWh in H2.
There were 19 commercial readings on hot days (≥25°C) with a mean consumption of 415.29 kWh.
The median consumption was 406.8 kWh (std dev 913.44 kWh). Mean temperature was 11.61°C. Commercial consumption showed a strong negative correlation with temperature (-0.64).

Peak tariff usage (599,624.07 kWh) was slightly lower than off-peak (608,075.89 kWh), accounting for 49.65% of total usage. 12 unique meters were tracked, with the highest single meter totaling 252,241.26 kWh.

limitations: Temperature data was missing for 62 readings, potentially affecting temperature-correlation accuracy.
The analysis relies on a single year of data, limiting the ability to assess year-over-year trends.
The high standard deviation relative to the mean suggests high variability in consumption per reading.
conclusion: Industrial consumption drives the majority of energy load. The increase in H2 usage and the negative correlation between temperature and commercial consumption suggest seasonal or operational shifts that warrant further investigation for load balancing.
